We therefore chose to err on the side of caution and collect 32 participants. This sample size was determined a priori in the preregistration. One participant was replaced for having a mean accuracy on the search task that was 3 SDs less than the group mean.

[PAPER_0060, relevance_score=0.278] Results

Search Trials

Trials with inaccurate responses (1.3%) and trials with RTs faster than 200 ms or slower than 2,000 ms (1.1%) were removed from search trial analysis, resulting in 2.3% of total trials removed. The singleton was present on every trial in this experiment to maximally incentivize suppression, and we therefore could not assess singleton-presence costs or benefits (but see Experiment 3 for RTs in the same task).

[PAPER_0065, relevance_score=0.192] There was not a significant difference in probe suppression effects between the display fill types, t(31) = 0.355, p = .725, dz = 0.06, suggesting that singletons were successfully suppressed for both filled and unfilled displays.

For transparency, an outlier participant had a -60.5% suppression effect (i.e., a large capture effect) in the filled condition that was 4.9 SDs from the group mean.

[PAPER_0066, relevance_score=0.271] If excluded, the basic pattern of results remains the same, except that the probe suppression effect is larger and more robust for filled displays (7.2%), t(30) = 6.33, p < .001, dz = 1.14. In short, excluding this outlier would not change the results and would only strengthen the observed probe suppression effect in the filled condition. In any case, the preregistration contained no a priori reason for excluding extreme outliers on probe report accuracy.

We also assessed whether the target shape was enhanced above baseline levels of the nonsingleton distractors.

[PREREG_0004, relevance_score=0.258] Study design

Participants will perform a capture-probe paradigm using stimuli adapted from Wang and Theeuwes (2020). On 75% of trials, participants will search for a specific target shape (e.g. circle) amongst a set of heterogenous shapes and report the location of a dot inside as quickly as possible (left vs. right). The colors, size, and shapes of the visual objects will match those of Wang and Theeuwes (2020). The color (green or red) and shape (circle or diamond) of the target will be counterbalanced across participants.

[PREREG_0005, relevance_score=0.229] On every trial, a color singleton will be presented at a nontarget location. Participants will be informed of this and will be instructed to ignore the color singleton. The location of the target and color singleton will be selected at random with the exception that they can never appear at the same location. On 25% of trials, participants will instead perform a probe task. After fixation, the search array will appear for 200 ms and then letters will be superimposed over the shapes for 100 ms before disappearing.

[PREREG_0007, relevance_score=0.260] Participants will not know whether a probe trial will occur. Probe trials will occur on a random subset of trials with the exception that probe trials cannot occur for two trials in a row. This is meant to maximize the probability of suppression effects by ensuring participants will have a strong attentional set from the search task on the previous trial. For one half of the experiment, the shapes will be filled with color (as in Gaspelin et al., 2015).

[PREREG_0008, relevance_score=0.233] For the other half of the experiment, the shapes will be unfilled outlines (as in Wang and Theeuwes, 2020). The order of these halves will be counterbalanced across participants. Each half will begin with a practice block with only search trials. Next, participants will perform a practice block with both probe and search trials. Finally, they will complete four experimental blocks with both probe and search trials intermixed.

Search Trials

Trials with inaccurate responses (1.3%) and trials with RTs faster than 200 ms or slower than 2,000 ms (1.1%) were removed from search trial analysis, resulting in 2.3% of total trials removed. The singleton was present on every trial in this experiment to maximally incentivize suppression, and we therefore could not assess singleton-presence costs or benefits (but see Experiment 3 for RTs in the same task).

Inference criteria

We will use p-values less than .05 on two-tailed t-tests as a test for statistical significance.

Data exclusion

All participants must be within 3 SDs of the group mean RT and accuracy on search trials to be included. If not, they will be replaced. All practice trials will be excluded. Search trials will be excluded from analyses if mean RT is less than 200 or greater than 2000 ms. Search trials will also be exclude from RT analyses if they are inaccurate.
